highlights.title: Tumble Forth – from assembly to OS with C compiler (2023)
highlights.summary: Tumble Forth is a 2023 project that builds a Forth system from assembly up to an OS using a C compiler.
highlights.detail: It demonstrates bootstrapping a language from low‑level code, includes a C compiler written in Forth, and can generate a minimal operating‑system image.

highlights.title: Building an Analog Geiger Counter
highlights.summary: A guide shows how to build an analog Geiger counter using a microcontroller with a display and digital readout.
highlights.detail: The design incorporates a Geiger‑Müller tube, a simple high‑voltage regulator, and the microcontroller reports counts per minute, offering hobbyists a low‑cost radiation detector.

highlights.title: From Atari to EVE Online: Building on 15 Years of AI Research in Games
highlights.summary: DeepMind is partnering with game studios to prototype AI-driven gameplay.
highlights.detail: The collaboration builds on fifteen years of DeepMind research from Atari to EVE Online, aiming to test novel agents in commercial titles and explore new gameplay mechanics.

highlights.title: Security updates for Friday
highlights.summary: LWN reports Friday security updates across major Linux distributions, covering dozens of packages such as Chromium, OpenSSH, and kernel.
highlights.detail: The updates address multiple CVEs, include kernel and library patches, and administrators are urged to apply them promptly to maintain system security.

highlights.title: EsotericSoftware/spine-runtimes
highlights.summary: The spine-runtimes repository provides C++ runtimes for 2D skeletal animation with Spine.
highlights.detail: The open‑source runtimes support multiple languages and enable developers to integrate Spine animations into games and interactive applications.

items.title: Model: empero-ai/Qwen3.8-27B-Ridge-GGUF
items.summary: The Qwen3.8-27B-Ridge model on Hugging Face has 27 billion parameters and targets image‑text‑to‑text tasks.
items.detail: It is distributed in the GGUF format for efficient local inference, excels at generating captions from images, and its popularity is reflected in the high download and like counts.

items.title: Model: orcarouter/Qwen3.8-27B-Uncensored-GGUF
items.summary: The Qwen3.8-27B-Uncensored model on Hugging Face has 27 billion parameters and targets image‑text‑to‑text tasks without safety filters.
items.detail: This uncensored variant removes content restrictions, allowing unrestricted generation, and is also provided in the GGUF format for fast on‑device use.

items.title: Model: ornith-ai/Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B
items.summary: Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B is a 35 billion‑parameter text generation model on Hugging Face.
items.detail: The model uses the A3B architecture, is fine‑tuned for instruction following, and is gaining traction among developers needing large‑scale language generation.

items.title: [$] Considering the OpenMDW license
items.summary: The OpenMDW license, proposed to the OSI by the Linux Foundation, seeks to define open‑source terms for LLM models, data, and weights.
items.detail: OpenMDW treats model weights as source code, aiming for clear licensing, but the proposal faces debate over compatibility with existing open‑source definitions.

items.title: Building a Hammond Organ to Understand How They Work
items.summary: A Hackaday article details constructing a Hammond organ to explore its electromechanical operation.
items.detail: The build recreates the tonewheel and rotary speaker mechanisms, helping readers understand how the instrument generates its characteristic sound.

items.title: Hacking A Cat Litter Box
items.summary: A Hackaday project modifies a Litter Robot 4 to add custom automation and odor control.
items.detail: Modifications include sensors for litter level detection and integration with home‑automation platforms to trigger alerts and improve odor management.

items.title: How the Grid’s Harmonic Filters Keep the Power Clean
items.summary: The article explains how harmonic filters are used in national power grids to reduce electrical distortion.
items.detail: Harmonic filters, composed of tuned inductors and capacitors, mitigate specific frequency components, improving power quality for sensitive industrial and consumer equipment.

items.title: OpenHD/OpenHD
items.summary: OpenHD is a C++ project listed on GitHub trending.
items.detail: The repository appears under the C++ language tag on GitHub's trending page, indicating recent community interest.

items.title: PostHog/posthog
items.summary: PostHog offers a platform with AI observability, analytics, session replay, feature flags, experiments, error tracking, and logs, controllable via Slack, web, desktop, or MCP.
items.detail: Positioned as a leading tool for building self‑driving products, it consolidates multiple developer‑experience features into a single interface.

items.title: Tencent/AI-Infra-Guard
items.summary: AI‑Infra‑Guard is a full‑stack AI red‑team platform that secures ecosystems through Agent, Skills, MCP, AI Infra scans and LLM jailbreak evaluation.
items.detail: Developed by Tencent, the platform provides comprehensive scanning capabilities to assess and harden AI infrastructure against adversarial attacks.

items.title: UE4SS-RE/RE-UE4SS
items.summary: RE‑UE4SS provides an injectable Lua scripting system, SDK generator, live property editor, and dumping utilities for Unreal Engine 4/5 games.
items.detail: Targeted at modders, the C++‑based tools enable runtime code injection and inspection of UE4/5 game assets.

items.title: Wei-Shaw/sub2api
items.summary: Sub2API is an open‑source relay service that unifies Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, and Grok subscriptions, enabling shared usage and cost splitting.
items.detail: The one‑stop platform supports car‑pool‑style sharing to distribute costs more efficiently while allowing native tools to operate seamlessly.
